newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel provident funds post positive returns.
newsitem.headline: Israel provident funds post positive returns.

text.p: Israel's much battered provident funds posted positive real returns in September as stock prices rose during most of the month, the top banks which manage the funds reported.
Bank Hapoalim, Israel's biggest bank, said its nine funds posted average real returns of 2.0 percent last month, after taking into account September's inflation of 0.4 percent.
But in the first nine months only two funds had positive real returns while the others posted negative returns ranging from -0.6 percent to -1.9 percent.
Bank Leumi's 14 funds had positive real returns in September ranging from 1.23 percent to 3.31 percent but in the first nine months only three of the funds had positive real returns.

Israel Discount Bank said its nine funds also all had positive real returns in September but since the beginning of the year only two funds had positive real returns. The others had negative returns ranging from -0.98 percent to -3.88.

Provident funds, long-term savings funds with special tax benefits, are among the most popular forms of investment in Israel. For more than a year, however, the funds have performed poorly due to the weak local securities market.
As a result, the funds have been hit with massive public redemptions.
